summary: Implement CS-CLOUD-IAM-004: Cloud IAM hot-path API and Cedar bind use-case requests now carry a shared typed tenant/cell/region placement boundary, reject missing cell/region or tenant drift before authorization, idempotency ledger writes, or domain mutation, and include placement in mutation idempotency fingerprints.

baseline_diff.before: Cloud IAM API/app requests carried raw tenant strings but no typed cell/region execution boundary; placement lived only in manifest/runbook doctrine.
baseline_diff.red_test: cargo test -p oya-cloud-iam-api iam_api_rejects_missing_typed_cell_or_region_boundary_before_ledger -- --nocapture failed before implementation with unresolved typed boundary structs/fields and placement-specific API errors.
baseline_diff.after: Shared domain placement newtypes back API boundary contexts and the Cedar bind use-case request. Boundary validation rejects empty cell/region and tenant drift before auth/domain/idempotency work; idempotency fingerprints include typed placement metadata. Existing tenant mismatch tests keep placement and header tenant synchronized to prove downstream tenant binding remains intact.

Placement metadata is explicit at the request boundary so blast-radius/cell routing cannot be an implicit ambient assumption.
Tests cover missing cell, missing region, placement tenant drift before authorization/domain mutation, and idempotency fingerprint drift on cell change.
Tests construct placement through a helper while production request structs keep explicit typed fields.
RED/GREEN tests, scoped Cloud IAM package tests, clippy, and fmt passed.

Share typed placement newtypes from the domain crate
F6_alternatives.selected_rationale: Shared domain value objects keep clean dependency direction and make API/app use-case boundaries explicit.
rejected_reasons: Manifest-only placement would not prevent hot-path execution without cell/region context.
Duplicate structs would drift across API and app seams.

findings: Tenant drift between header/request and typed placement is rejected before authorization decisions or IAM mutation.
Validation is trim/equality only; no I/O or registry lookup on hot paths.
Audit-chain row records the typed placement boundary implementation evidence.
Additive request boundary fields and tests are local to Cloud IAM domain/app/API crates.
New stable API/app errors distinguish missing cell, missing region, and tenant placement drift.
Cell and region IDs now travel with request metadata and response metadata for the app bind seam.
API/app validate boundary metadata before translating into IAM domain operations; domain business logic remains separate.
Clean architecture direction preserved: shared domain value objects, API/app validation at their request boundaries, no API dependency from app/domain.
API and app regressions prove boundary metadata cannot be omitted or drift from tenant context before mutation.
Evidence records RED/GREEN, scoped Cloud IAM verification, and hyperscaler cell-placement references.

best_practice_research.question: How should hyperscaler-style IAM hot paths carry tenant/cell/region placement context?
best_practice_research.direct_recommendation: Make tenant/cell/region explicit typed boundary metadata on hot-path requests and validate it before authorization or state mutation; do not rely on manifest-only or ambient routing context.

evidence_used.establishes: cell boundaries and shuffle-sharding reduce blast radius when tenant/customer placement is explicit
cell-based architecture is an AWS resiliency pattern for bounded workload placement
zone/region placement is a first-class resiliency boundary, not an implicit implementation detail

repo_local_context: ADR-0009 requires per-tenant per-region cells and request cell_id propagation.
ADR-0244 makes tenant the universal scoping primitive while retaining home_cell/dr_cell binding.
CS-CLOUD-IAM-004 requires typed tenant/cell/region boundary metadata for IAM hot paths.
boundaries_non_goals: This slice does not implement cell routing or tenancy registry lookups.
